title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): second way — reprobation to damnation without gaze on disobedience hates the creature without justice-love and kills hope in God
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, because (as they say) it establishes that God has predestined some men unto damnation without the intuit of disobedience: whence again it follows that God hates his creature apart from any necessity from love toward justice: Which being posited, hope in God is taken away. For he who certainly persuades himself that he has been reprobated from salvation apart from the intuit of sin will believe that nothing can profit him, howsoever he strive to avoid sin.
pass_b_english: Second: as they say, it sets God as having predestined some men to damnation without any gaze on disobedience — from which again it follows that God hates his creature with no necessity arising from love of justice. That granted, hope in God is taken away. For whoever is sure he has been reprobated from salvation apart from any gaze on sin will believe nothing can profit him, however hard he strives to avoid sin.
source_text: Secundo, quia (ut illi aiunt) statuit Deus aliquos homines ad damnationem praedestinasse sine intuitu inobedientiae: unde rursus sequitur, Deum creaturam suam odisse citra nullam ex amore erga justitiam necessitatem: Quo posito, tollitur spes in Deum. Qui enim certe sibi persuadet se a salute citra peccati intuitum esse reprobatum, credet nihil sibi posse prodesse, quomodocunque studeat peccatum vitare.
